b: The Indian Burial Ground is a common trope in American folklore. Usually, it involves a house/building/etc being haunted or cursed, with the curse/haunting being caused by the fact that it was built over a Native American gravesite (or sometimes a holy site, if the storyteller is being a bit more creative).

I've been watching and reading a good amount of older horror media lately, and have run across this trope several times. It is popular enough that people make fun of its overuse as a slightly cheesy (as well as mildly racist) trope. What I want to know is where and when this trope originated. The oldest mention of it which I can find is Philip Freneau's 1787 poem "The Indian Burial Ground". The poem isn't a part of the horror genre, as many uses of this trope are. Did it originally have non-horror beginnings and then became a horror trope via popular stories? And is Freneau's poem the actual earliest mention of this or did it exist in folklore before that? I also would love to see more early examples of this trope just to see how the handling of this type of story has evolved over the years. Thank you!
